rites.name: Miamaerys
rites.text: Miamaerys is the concept of the first sounding of Ryenaerlae, the note held before form existed, when the earliest roots of the world began to condense out of resonance. It is not a being in the ordinary sense but a standing pitch that other things later learned to tune themselves against.

rites.name: Brurneld
rites.text: Brurneld is the concept of resonance that rang through the Singing, when the first roots of Ryenaerlae gathered out of silence. It is not a being but the pattern by which the world first learned to hold its shape.

rites.name: Maunastes
rites.text: Maunastes is the concept of the Singing, the sound that rang out as the first roots of Ryenaerlae condensed out of the dark. In the Holy Age its name is spoken by flame-keepers and temple orders as the origin of all things that can be heard.

rites.name: Seriallor
rites.text: Seriallor is the concept of the sounding that brings the first roots of Ryenaerlae into being, a resonance felt as a low hum beneath all things during the Holy Age of flame and temple orders. It is not a single being but the pattern by which the world's foundations take hold and begin to ring.

rites.name: Sishora
rites.text: Sishora is the concept of the Weave in the Seeding, the stage when makers plant threads of latent power into the fabric of Ryenaerlae. It holds the quiet promise of powers that have not yet woken, a pattern waiting for its first rising.

rites.name: Roneoses
rites.text: Roneoses is a quiet concept of the Weave, the living lattice the makers plant in the Seeding while the old powers sleep beneath the groves. It is said to hold the memory of first sovereigns and to stir only when a grove is cut or a kingdom grows too proud.

rites.name: Kruthoggoth
rites.text: Kruthoggoth is the concept of the living sap that ran beneath the broken roots of Ryenaerlae, the force the first sovereign drew upon when the groves were first tended. In the Sundering it was said to bind the shards of fractured worlds back into the groundwork of the Pact. It is remembered less as a being than as a rule the growing kingdoms learned to obey.

rites.name: Cestintor
rites.text: Cestintor is the Arcane concept of binding, the thread by which a sworn oath held worlds together during the Sundering. In the Age of Sundering it was invoked when landfall broke old bonds and shards drifted free of the Pact.

rites.name: Shazeth
rites.text: Shazeth is the concept of the holding wall, the idea that a boundary can be kept by will and stone alike, and it shaped the Walled Age of Ryenaerlae. Its first crossings were recorded as the moment a people chose to remain behind a line rather than leave it. It is named in the orders that still keep the old gates.

rites.name: Miinaelae
rites.text: Miinaelae is a concept of Ryenaerlae, understood in the Walled Age as the principle that a boundary can hold back what is beyond it. Its adherents raised walls, sworn orders and churches to keep the grove-kingdoms apart, and the first crossings were made when someone learned to pass through a wall without breaking it.

rites.name: Amarnirium
rites.text: Amarnirium is a concept of the Walled Age in Ryenaerlae, an idea of enclosure and held ground that shaped the orders and churches of that time. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds, it became the frame through which people judged which walls should stand and which should fall.

rites.name: Silaennys
rites.text: Silaennys is a sealed, lattice-bound working of Arcane craft in the Ryenaerlae, a standing spell-form kept by the Thirteen Quiet Hands of the third age. Its wielders trace its patterns through rings of cold glass, and the form is said to bloom only when a caster accepts its full cost.

rites.name: Coreolistum
rites.text: Coreolistum is the concept of Ryenaerlae held within the Three Futures, the moment when the ending forks into branches and the Library of Arcane Record shelves each outcome as its own volume. It is not a place or a being but the idea that every unrealized path still has weight. Those who read it say it hums like a chord that never resolves.
